etymology.historical_story: English cheese continues Old English forms such as cēse, ultimately connected through Germanic borrowing with Latin cāseus. In Malaysian conversation, the English word can appear inside a Malay sentence, while keju supplies the standard Malay equivalent. The pairing is a useful reminder that shared food references do not require identical spellings across languages. [English etymology](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/cheese); [DBP equivalence](https://dewanbahasa.jendeladbp.my/2024/05/03/13225/).

etymology.historical_story: English cipher ultimately comes from Arabic ṣifr, meaning empty or zero, through medieval European forms. A word associated with numerical notation later developed a connection with secret writing. Its modern technical sense concerns encryption systems. Malay terminology uses sifer for this concept, while the original English spelling often appears alongside it in bilingual technical material. [Word history](https://www.etymonline.com/word/cipher).
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 cipher 读成“赛弗”，想象一封信被换成看不懂的符号；马来语技术词记作 sifer。

etymology.historical_story: English chief reached Middle English through Anglo-French chief or chef, ultimately from Latin caput, meaning head. The body metaphor helps connect a group's leader with the highest office and the most important matter. Malay normally expresses these meanings with ketua or utama; encountering chief in conversation does not itself establish a naturalized Malay word. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/chief)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 读 /tʃiːf/，把 chief 想成站在队伍最前面的负责人：用于人是“首领”，用于职位是“首席”，用于事情是“主要”。

senses.en_definition: Remote computing resources and services accessed over a network, especially the internet; the cloud.
senses.ms_definition: Dalam penggunaan istilah Inggeris, sumber dan perkhidmatan pengkomputeran jarak jauh yang dicapai melalui rangkaian, khususnya Internet; padanan bahasa Melayunya ialah awan.
senses.nuances: 此处记录英语技术词在马来语交流中的混用，不认定 cloud 为规范马来语词。正式马来文使用 awan、pengkomputeran awan 或 storan awan。status 按指定格式保留为 official，不代表 DBP 已认可 cloud 为马来语词头。马来文释义为编辑说明，并非 DBP 对 cloud 的直接释义。英语本义“云”对应 awan；本条不将英语的全部义项列为马来语义项。术语依据见 [DBP：pengkomputeran awan](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=pengkomputeran)。

etymology.historical_story: The computing use of cloud draws on network diagrams in which a cloud shape represents the internet while leaving its internal infrastructure unspecified. Malay expresses the same metaphor with awan. DBP explains this diagrammatic connection in its account of pengkomputeran awan. When speakers retain English cloud in Malay conversation, they carry that technical metaphor across languages without translating the word.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: cloud /klaʊd/ 就是英语“云”：把远端服务器画成一朵云，文件传过去就是存入云端；规范马来语对应 awan。

etymology.historical_story: The supplied dictionary does not establish the origin of conor. Its documented interest lies in fish naming: one local name can cover more than one scientific identification. Malaysian fisheries guides use the fuller name conor curut for Saurida tumbil. This shows why a market name and a biological species name need not have identical boundaries. [LKIM](https://www.lkim.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Buku-Ikan-Ikan-Komersial-Di-Malaysia.pdf)

etymology.historical_story: Carlton belongs to a family of English place names associated with settlements of free peasants. Historical explanations connect ceorl or Scandinavian karl with tūn, meaning a settlement or estate. These place names also supplied surnames. This background explains the name's formation, but cannot identify which person, place, or organization the supplied token denotes. See [Carlton Parish Council](https://www.carltonpc.co.uk/files/Carlton%20Place%20Names.pdf).

etymology.historical_story: Cebisan belongs to the Malay word family built around cebis, a small scrap or fragment. The suffix -an names the resulting piece. Its everyday imagery is easy to picture: torn paper or leftover cloth. In reflective writing, the same image extends to memories and life stories, presenting an incomplete recollection as something preserved from a larger whole.

etymology.historical_story: The compound brings together cita and rasa, linking inclination with sensory experience. Its dictionary meanings range from food flavour to personal preference, allowing the same expression to describe a dish, a wardrobe or a television programme. This connection offers a useful cultural bridge between tasting something and finding it personally appealing. Standard Malaysian spelling keeps the two words separate. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=175768&keyword=cita+rasa)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 抓住 rasa“感觉、味道”：舌头喜欢的是风味，心里喜欢的是品味；两种意思都用 cita rasa。

etymology.historical_story: Cowok is associated with colloquial Indonesian rather than formal Malaysian address. Uri Tadmor’s Indonesian vocabulary in the World Loanword Database analyses it as a back-formation from céwék, meaning woman, while treating cowok itself as morphologically unanalysable. Kamus Dewan records both the young-man and boyfriend senses, preserving its conversational character. [Sources: WOLD](https://wold.clld.org/word/71261839426667229), [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/cari1?keyword=cowok).

etymology.historical_story: English creasy combines crease with the adjective-forming suffix -y. Collins dates this formation to 1855–1860. This English history does not establish a Malay borrowing, and the packet supplies no contextual evidence identifying its original occurrence. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/creasy)

etymology.historical_story: As a drink name, Coke became a registered Coca-Cola trademark in 1945. English also has lowercase coke meaning an industrial fuel or, in slang, cocaine. These meanings must be distinguished by context rather than merged into one origin story. In Malay ordering conversations, the capitalized brand name identifies the beverage. [Brand history](https://www.coca-colacompany.com/about-us/history/the-asa-candler-era); [English senses](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/coke).

etymology.historical_story: Kamus Dewan records cal as a colloquial clothing word and explains it through selendang, mafela, sal, syal, and cala. This places it within vocabulary for wrapping or draping cloth around the body. The available evidence does not establish its borrowing route or earliest use, so a specific foreign origin cannot responsibly be assigned. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=274404&keyword=cal)

etymology.historical_story: Chandramukhi is associated with Sanskrit Candramukhī, conventionally interpreted as a woman whose face resembles the moon. The image connects a name with a poetic comparison rather than a literal description. Its appearance in a Malay text may identify a person or fictional character; it does not establish a Malay common noun. Reference: [Candramukhī dictionary material](https://www.wisdomlib.org/definition/candramukhi).

etymology.historical_story: English chick developed as a shortened form of chicken, according to Oxford’s etymological note. Its literal meaning concerns a young bird, while a separate informal use refers to a young woman. When the word appears inside a Malay conversation, it may simply represent English code-switching; that appearance alone does not establish an official Malay borrowing. [Source: Oxford Learner’s Dictionaries](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/chick?q=chick).

etymology.historical_story: Celana carries a trace of clothing exchange across the Indian Ocean. Research on port communities connects it with Kannada or Tulu callaṇa, meaning short breeches. Garments and their names travelled together through maritime contact. In Malay, the borrowed word became an independent noun and acquired the regular derivative bercelana, meaning to wear trousers. [Research](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0165115318000645).

etymology.historical_story: English crore comes from Hindi karoṛ, ultimately based on Sanskrit koṭi, meaning ten million. It preserves a South Asian way of naming large quantities alongside lakh, meaning one hundred thousand. For Malaysian readers encountering Indian news or film earnings, the cultural bridge is numerical: translate the counting unit before interpreting the amount or its currency. [Reference: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/crore)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 /krɔːr/ 记成整块声音，再牢绑定“千万”：1 crore = 10 million；先记单位，别把它当货币。

etymology.historical_story: Cincang is linked in Kamus Dewan to cencang, a word for repeated chopping with a blade. Its cultural reach extends beyond the kitchen: the proverb air dicencang, tiada putus pictures water that cannot be severed, expressing how family ties survive quarrels. This is a documented cultural association, rather than proof of a particular ancient origin. See [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=244840&keyword=cencang).

etymology.historical_story: Cewek illustrates how closely related language communities can share vocabulary while assigning it different registers. Kamus Dewan records an Indonesian-marked colloquial meaning, a young woman, alongside the girlfriend meaning. For Malaysian learners, that contrast matters more than a speculative ancient origin: a word encountered in Indonesian dialogue may be understood locally yet still sound informal. The cited entry does not establish an earlier derivation. [DBP](https://prpm.dbp.gov.my/Cari1?d=73980&keyword=teman+wanita)

morphology.pattern_note: 词根无词缀；meN- 遇 c 通常变为 men-，保留 c，形成 mencekik。词尾 k 常读作喉塞音 [ʔ]；部分马来西亚口音将末音节读作 [keʔ]。

etymology.historical_story: Cekik offers a vivid example of bodily experience shaping Malay metaphor. Its literal image is a throat held so tightly that breathing becomes difficult. The same word family describes poverty and exploitation as pressures that leave people struggling for air. The established expression mencekik darah turns that image into a forceful criticism of oppressive charges or demands.
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把 cekik 末尾突然收住的 [ʔ] 当作“气被卡住”的声音提示：掐住脖子，再联想到价格压得人喘不过气。

etymology.historical_story: The English machine name developed through a visual comparison with the crane bird: a lifting machine's projecting arm suggested a long neck. That connection belongs to English word history. For Malaysian Malay, the useful distinction is between English crane in mixed conversation and kren in standard terminology. [Word-origin reference](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/crane_1).

etymology.historical_story: Christina developed from Christiana, the Latin feminine form associated with Christian. Related spellings travelled across European languages, including Cristina and Kristina. In a Malay sentence, Christina functions simply as someone's name, with its spelling normally preserved. Its historical religious association does not establish the beliefs of a present-day bearer. See [Behind the Name](https://www.behindthename.com/name/christina).

etymology.historical_story: Cinderella belongs to an international family of tales about a persecuted heroine whose fortunes change. Charles Perrault published his influential French Cendrillon in 1697, while the Brothers Grimm later recorded Aschenputtel. The ash-associated names recall the heroine’s lowly domestic position. The English name also supplies a metaphor for unexpected success. [University of Illinois background](https://csames.illinois.edu/system/files/2020-12/Cinderella_Background_Information.pdf)
etymology.cognitive_memory_aid: 把英语 cinder“灰烬”与炉边受委屈的女孩连起来：Cinderella 就是“灰姑娘”。这是词源联想，不是马来语构词拆分。
